newsitem.title: UK: Dividend wariness dampens Brit Gas enthusiasm.
newsitem.headline: Dividend wariness dampens Brit Gas enthusiasm.

text.p: Wariness over British Gas' dividend prospects dampened initial enthusiasm over a new gas supply contract with British Petroleum, analysts said on Thursday.
British Gas' comments during the analysts' meeting gave rise to fairly bleak expectations for the dividend once the company has completed its planned demerger.
The break-up will involve a separate listing for the firm's trading arm, to be called Centrica, while British Gas will be renamed BG plc.
"The main surprise today was the unveiling of BG's dividend mechanism," said Kleinwort Benson analyst Paul Spedding.
British Gas said BG's dividend would be funded out of the the profit from TransCo, the pipeline transport business and BG's main asset.
The dividend will be paid out of TransCo's current cost profit after servicing its regulatory capital and after taxation.
BG's business will also include exploration and production and international downstream operations, but these will be self-financing.
Analysts said that British Gas indicated if this planed dividend policy had been applied last year the pay-out would have been a mere 5.7 pence a share.
British Gas actually paid a dividend in 1995 of 14.5 pence, which will be maintained this year.

While acknowledging there were too many uncertainties to take the 5.7 pence as a firm guideline for BG dividends in coming years, the figure nevertheless raised concern, analysts said. "You've got to acknowledge there is a possibility that the dividend will be halved," said Daniel Martin at BZW.
British Gas shares initially peaked at 231-1/2, but eventually close4-1/2 pence up at 220-1/2.
News of a breakthrough in the take-or-pay talks helped the shares early on as the market breathed a sigh of relief that British Gas had found an opening to tackle the problem.
The utility said it would pay a total 293 million pounds to its own production unit and to British Petroleum, which will give British Gas relief on gas prices and volumes it has to lift.
British Gas said the two deals solved about 10 percent of its total take-or-pay problem.

Lacking further clues, analysts made a crude calculation to find that a complete solution to the take-or-pay problem would roughly cost a gross three billion pounds or two billion once it was offset against taxable profits.
While analysts were divided on whether this was, or was not, a large amount, the figures do give an important indication as to the value of part of British Gas assets, BZW's Martin said.
"We've got more of handle now than we had before," he said.

Martin added that -- given the uncertainties over BG's dividend and the fact Centrica will not make any pay-outs at all in the near future -- it was better to value British Gas shares on an asset rather than on a dividend yield basis as used to be the case.
In doing so, he estimated that British Gas was worth about 290 pence per share.
"Basically, I'm more positive than I was this morning," he said.
